newsitem.title: ITALY: Genoa aims to be main Mediterranean container port.
newsitem.headline: Genoa aims to be main Mediterranean container port.

text.p: Italy's port of Genoa aims to become the Mediterranean's main container port in 1997 with over one million containers moved, port authority chairman Giuliano Gallanti said.

He said the port, which recently became Italy's only completely privatised port with 19 companies in charge of management, will move 800,000 TEU (20 foot equivalent) containers this year, up 138 percent on 1993.
This equalled nearly 13 million tonnes of goods, up 64 percent on 1993, he told a news conference. Ferry and cruise ship traffic was up 96 percent on 1993, he added.
Port employees totalled 2,340, down from 8,513 in 1983.
The port planned to make investments of some $380 million in the 1996-98 period, of which $145 million would come from the private sector.
A free zone bonded area was also planned.

Recently published figures from Censis research body showed Italy's maritime industry as a whole was the nation's sixth largest industrial sector, accounting for 2.6 percent of gross domestic product.

The survey, based on 1994 data, showed annual turnover equalled some 42 trillion lire, of which 40 percent was export-linked. The industry, employing a total of over 300,000, was growing by about 2.5 percent a year.
